questions.question: In the context of Buddhist architecture, what is a ‘chaitya’?

options.text: A hall for prayer and assembly

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**a hall for prayer and assembly**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• A 'chaitya' is a Buddhist prayer hall with a stupa at one end, used for congregational worship and assembly.
 
• These halls are characterized by their apsidal (semi-circular) end and barrel-vaulted roofs.
 
• Chaityas are typically carved out of rock in cave complexes, such as those in Ajanta and Ellora in India.
 
• The architecture of chaityas includes pillars that divide the hall into a central nave and aisles on either side.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Stupa**

 
 
• A stupa is a dome-shaped structure that contains relics and is used as a place of meditation.
 
• Stupas are significant in Buddhist culture, symbolizing the enlightened mind of the Buddha.
 
 
 
• **Vihara**
 
 
• Vihara refers to a Buddhist monastery, often consisting of living quarters for monks.
 
• These structures also include a central courtyard and cells for individual monks.
 
 
 
• **Ajanta and Ellora Caves**
 
 
• The Ajanta and Ellora caves are renowned for their rock-cut architecture and intricate carvings.
 
• These caves feature several chaityas and viharas, dating back to ancient India.
 
 
 
• **Barrel Vault**
 
 
• A barrel vault is a semi-cylindrical structure, forming a continuous arch.
 
• This architectural element is commonly found in chaityas, providing a spacious and acoustically resonant interior.

questions.question: On the shores of the Bay of Bengal, the temple at Konark was built in the ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**13th**____** century**__.

__
 
• **On the shores of the Bay of Bengal, the temple at Konark was built in the 13th**** century**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

 
• Konark Sun Temple, located in the **East Odisha** near the sacred **city of Puri**.
 
• Built in the 13th year by King Narasimha I (AD 1238-1264).
 
• Its scale, refinement and concept represent the strength and stability of the Ganga Empire as well as the value systems of the historical environment.
 
• The temple is designed in the shape of a** colossal chariot**.
 
• It is dedicated to the god sun.
 
• In this sense, it is directly and materially linked to Brahmanism and tantric belief systems.
 
• The Konark temple is widely known not only for its architectural grandeur but also for the intricacy and profusion of sculptural work.
 
• It marks the highest point of achievement of Kalinga architecture depicting the grace, the joy and the rhythm of life all its wondrous variety.
 
• **It was declared a UNESCO world heritage site in 1984.**
 
• There are two rows of **12 wheels on each side of the Konark sun temple**.
 
• Sailors once called this Sun Temple of Konark, the Black Pagoda because it was supposed to draw ships into the shore and cause shipwrecks.
 
• Konârak is the invaluable link in the history of the diffusion of the cult of Surya, which originating in Kashmir during the 8th century, finally reached the shores of Eastern India.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example Monolithic Architecture?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Dharmraj Rath of Mahabalipuram**__.

__
 
• Dharmaraja Ratha is a monument in the Pancha Ratha complex at **Mahabalipuram** on the **Coromandel Coast of the Bay of Bengal in the Kancheepuram district **of the Indian state of Tamil Nadu.

 
 
• **It is an example of monolithic Indian rock-cut architecture**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• **Monolithic architecture **refers to free-standing structures made from a** single piece of material**. 

 
 
• Monolithic architecture, like the Ellora Kailasanathar temple, is often rock-cut, but monolithic structures can also be cast from artificial materials such as concrete.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The** Mahabodhi Temple, **a UNESCO World Heritage Site, is an ancient Buddhist temple in **Bodh Gaya**.
 
• **Brihadisvara Temple**, locally known as Thanjai Periya Kovil, and also known as Rajarajeshwaram, is a Hindu Dravidian-style temple dedicated to Lord Shiva located on the south bank of the Kaveri River in **Thanjavur**, Tamil Nadu.
 
• **Arulmigu Meenakshi Amman Temple **is located on the southern bank of the Vaigai River in the temple city of Madurai, Tamil Nadu, India.
 
 
• It is dedicated to Goddess Meenakshi, a form of Parvati, and his consort, Sundareswarar, a form of Shiva.

questions.question: Battered walls are a distinctive feature of the architecture of the _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Tughlaqs.__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **__Important Points__**

__
 
• The general features of the Tughlaq style of architecture are-
 
 
• **Stone rubble** is the principal building material and the walls are in most cases plastered.
 
• **The walls and bastions are invariably battered, the effect is most marked at the corners. Hence, option 1 is the correct answer.**
 
• A hesitant and possibly experimental use of a new shape of arch – the four centered arch-necessitating its reinforcement with a supporting beam.
 
• This **arch-beam** combination is a hall-mark of the Tughlaq style.
 
• The pointed **horse-shoe arch** of the preceding style was abandoned because of its narrow compass and therefore the inability to span wider spaces.
 
• Emergence of a** pointed dome** with clearly visible neck in contrast with rather stifled dome of the preceding style.
 
• Introduction of **encaustictiles **as an element of decoration in the panels of the buildings.
 
• The emergence of an** octagonal plan**, in the tombs of this period, came to be copied and perfected by the Mughals in the 16th-17th century.
 
• An additional feature was the element of reduced ornament, confined mostly to inscribed borders and medallions in spandrels executed in plaster or stucco. 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• After the fall of the **Khilji dynasty**, a new dynasty emerged in Delhi which is called **Tughlaq Dynasty. **
 
• The Tughlaq Dynasty ruled Delhi from 1320 to 1413 AD. 
 
• The first ruler of the Tughlaq dynasty was Ghazi Malik, who introduced himself as his **Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq**.

questions.question: Which one of the following is an example of rock cut temple architecture?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kailasha Temple of Ellora**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Kailasha Temple** at Ellora is a unique example of rock-cut temple architecture, carved entirely out of a single rock.
 
• It is part of the **Ellora Caves**, a UNESCO World Heritage Site located in Maharashtra, India.
 
• The temple is dedicated to Lord Shiva and is inspired by Mount Kailash, the abode of Shiva.
 
• Constructed during the reign of the **Rashtrakuta dynasty** in the 8th century CE, it showcases advanced engineering and artistic skills.
 
• The temple is notable for its **monolithic structure**, intricate carvings, and elaborate sculptures, making it a masterpiece of ancient Indian architecture.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Rock-Cut Architecture:** It involves carving structures into natural rock formations, often used for temples, monasteries, and caves.
 
• **Ellora Caves:** A complex of 34 caves consisting of Buddhist, Hindu, and Jain monuments, reflecting India's diverse religious traditions.
 
• **Monolithic Architecture:** Refers to structures carved out of a single piece of rock, ensuring durability and artistic unity.
 
• **Rashtrakuta Dynasty:** Known for their patronage of art and architecture, they ruled large parts of India during the 8th to 10th centuries CE.
 
• The Kailasha Temple is often compared to other ancient architectural marvels like the **Petra in Jordan** and the **Great Pyramids of Egypt** for its engineering ingenuity.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a correct match for Buddhist Architecture?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chaityas – Tree.**__

** Correct match for Buddhist Architecture**

 
 

 Stambhas

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Chaityas - Sacred spots**

 
 
• **​**The word chaitya is derived from 'Chita', meaning funeral pyre, and by extension a funeral mound.
 
• Chaityas were the places of worship and assembly of monks and contain stupas within the structure at one end.
 
• Chaityas were essential to those in Buddhism who gathered for worship.
 
• They have a small rectangular door that opens into the domed hall, which is called the Chaitya Hall.
 
• The early Chaityas are examples of Indian rock-cut architecture, Which was built inside the cave.
 
• Some famous rock-cut chaityas at Bhaja, Nasik, Karli, Ajanta, and Ellora.
 
 

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• **Stupas – Topes**

 
 
• **​**Buddha's relics such as his bodily remains or the objects he used were buried there, these were mounds known as stupas.
 
• The stupa (In Sanskrit meaning a heap) originated as a simple semi-circular mound of earth. 
 
• Gradually, it evolved into a more complex structure, balancing round and square shapes.
 
• Above the stupa was the Harmika, a balcony-like structure that represented the abode of the gods.
 
 
 
• Some famous stupas in India are:

 
 

 Mahabodhi Stupa
 Bodh Gaya
 
 

 Sanchi Stupa
 Madhya Pradesh
 
 

 Shanti Stupa
 Leh
 
 

 Dhamekh Stupa
 Sarnath
 
 

 Kesaria Stupa
 Bihar
 
 

 Maha Stupa
 Thotlakunda
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/5a9cbb0d0ab914ba3540bf47ed6808f8f03acbf03839551daeecdf0f836d7296.png] 

 
• **Viharas – Monasteries**

 
 
• **​**This is an example of a rock-cut architect who used to be near the chaityas.
 
• It had a central square space, with or without pillars, surrounded by chambers for priests.
 
• Primarily it was a residential place for sages or Buddhist priests.
 
• Viharas were mostly constructed with brick or carved out of rocks.
 
• Some famous viharas are Nalanda Vihar, Odantpuri Vihar.
 
• **Kanha Caves viharas in the Nasik Caves, 1st century BCE, is one of the earliest.**
 
 Stambhas – Lats

 
 
• Stambha, or lay, was a type of pillar with carved inscriptions.
 
• It had symbols like elephant and lion on it.
 
• It also showed affiliation with Persepolitan architecture.

questions.question: Other than at Daulatabad, where in the Deccan can we find examples of Tughlaq architecture?
questions.solution:
Other than at Daulatabad, we can find examples of Tughlaq architecture at **__Khush Mahal in Warangal__** in the Deccan.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• 
 We can find the examples of **Tughlaq architecture at Daulatabad** when **Muhammad bin Tughlaq** moved his capital over there.
 
 
• 
 Other than **Daulatabad**, we can also find the examples of **Tughlaq architecture at Warangal **in **Deccan.**
 
 
• 
 **Khush Mahal in Warangal **is said to be built during **Tughlaq reign in 14th century.**
 
 
• 
 It is said to be built over the site of **Kakatiya palace****.**
 
 
• 
 Traces of Tughlaq architectural style is still seen on this structure.
 
 
• 
 For instance, the walls of the Mahal which are slightly inclined are indicative of the structural style of that period.
 
 
• 
 However, according to some it was built by **Shitab Khan**, the then Warangal Governor of **Qutub Shahi Dynasty.**
 
 
• 
 He then used Khush Mahal as an **auditorium**.
 
 
• 
 Hence, it is also known by the name of **Shitab Khan Mahal. **
 
 
• 
 It is said that **Prince Ulugh Khan of Tughlaq dynasty,** after conquering Warangal from Kakatiya rulers, started establishing the territory of Delhi Sultanate by demolishing **Kakatiya architectures** and building new structures.
 
 
• 
 It was then he built Khush Mahal, a short distance away from the gateways of the **Warangal fort.**
 
 
• 
 Khush Mahal structure resembles the **Diwan-i-aam of Tughlaqabad**, which is also a public audience hall.
 
 
• 
 
One can also find architectural similarity between Khush Mahal and **tomb of Giyas-ud-Din Tughluq of Delhi.**

 

Therefore, we can conclude that other than at Daulatabad, we can find examples of Tughlaq architecture at Khush Mahal in Warangal__ in the Deccan.

questions.question: Where is the first evidence of stone engraved architecture found?
questions.solution:
The first evidence of stone engraved architecture was found in **Lomas Rishi Caves.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ​The Barabar Caves in the Gaya district of Bihar state are the oldest rock-cut caves in India, most of which date back to the Maurya period (322–195 BCE) and some of which contain Ashoka's edicts.
 
• Four caves named Karan Chaupar, Lomas Rishi, Sudama and Vishwa Jhopri are made by cutting rocks in the equal hill.
 
• The Sudama and Lomas Rishi caves are the earliest examples of rock-cut cave architecture in India with architectural details dating back to the Mauryan period.
 
• The Lomas Rishi cave is in the form of an imitation of the contemporary architecture of a wooden arch-like shape. A row of elephants on the way to the gate advance along the arched door frames towards the stupa figures.

**Lomasa Rishi Cave****:-**

 
• It was carved out of gigantic rounded granite rock.
 
• It comprises two rooms i.e: a large hall and an assembly hall in a rectangular shape. 
 
 
• The assembly hall is an oval-shaped room with a roof in the form of a dome.
 
 
 
• The interior surfaces of the chambers have a remarkable glass-like polish.
 
 
• Polishing the caves from the inside & constructing the artistic gateway were the features added by the Mauryas.
 
 
 
• On the wall of the cave, there are inscriptions of the elephant and other motifs. No inscriptions related to Ashoka have been found **in the Lomas Rishi Cave. **

**​** [IMAGE: https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/2/26/Lomas_Rishi_Cave%2C_Barabar_Hills.jpg] [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
 

 **Ajanta Caves**
 
 
 
• These caves may be divided into two phases: Satavahana and Vakataka.
 
• Ajanta contains 30 Buddhist Caves.
 
• It was declared a World Heritage Site by UNESCO in 1983. 
 
 
 
 

 **Kailashnath Temple at Ellora**
 
 
 
• It is cave 16 of Ellora.
 
• It is the World's largest single monolithic discovery during the reign of the Rashtrakuta dynasty, Krishna 1.
